idee_recherchee.texte: At the centre of a black hole, the equations of general relativity break down into a singularity of infinite density, which shows that our current theories cannot fully describe what happens at extreme gravity.

titre_video: Scientists Are Freaking Out Over Space Time (It's Not Real)
titre: Que contient un trou noir ? Théories et perte d'information
resume: What lies inside a black hole is unknown because math and science break down past the event horizon. Theories include quantum effects near the singularity sending matter to another quantum realm or universe, a black hole eventually exploding after billions of years, and debate over whether information is stored in the singularity or destroyed forever.
texte: So, this brings us to one of the biggest mysteries in science. What is actually inside of a black hole? The short answer is scientists [music] just don't know. This is due to the fact that traditional math and science break down once you get past the event horizon. However, there are some theories of what might happen just past the maw of these cosmic behemoths. [music] Many scientists believe that as something gets close to the singularity of a black hole, quantum effects [music] that we just don't know about yet begin to take over. Could this cause the matter that falls past the event horizon [music] to end up in another quantum realm or a universe altogether? Scientists can't even [music] begin to make predictions due to the fact that we don't know what forces are at work near the singularity. There's evidence to suggest that all of the matter being incorporated into the singularity will eventually become so immense that the black hole itself could explode. [music] However, physicists have noted that it could take billions and billions of years for this to happen, even to the oldest black holes. Some scientists believe that the information pulled into black holes might be stored in the singularity, while others think that somehow the information is destroyed and gone forever.
